## Analysis Outline

**Placement Counts**

**Placement count and placements per 'case' over time**

* By pre-/post-adjudication

* By placement type

* By charge category

* By placement history

*	By race/ethnicity (RRI using MI population juvenile race/ethnicity data for pertinent counties)

* By age

* By gender

**Length of Stay**

**Mean and median length of stay over time** 

* By pre-/post-adjudication

* By placement type

* By charge category

* By placement history

*	By race/ethnicity (with t-tests for statistical significance of differences in means)

* By age

* By gender

**Other**

* There appears to be both "special cost" and "per diem" fields in the placement file

### 1. Read in Pertinent TCS Files for Placement Analysis: 'cases', 'charges', 'dispositions', and 'placements'
```{r message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### set sharepoint path using csgjcr::csg_sp_path function
sharepoint_tcs_data_path <- csg_sp_path("JC Research - JJ_Michigan - JJ_Michigan/Data/Raw/Courts/JIS/TCS")

### import cases
tcs_cases <- read_xlsx(
  file.path(
    sharepoint_tcs_data_path, "TCS_Cases_A.xlsx"),
  .name_repair = make_clean_names
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.POSIXct), as.Date))

### import charges
tcs_charges <- read_xlsx(
  file.path(
    sharepoint_tcs_data_path, "TCS_Charges_A.xlsx"),
  .name_repair = make_clean_names
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.POSIXct), as.Date))

### import dispositions
tcs_dispositions <- read_xlsx(
  file.path(
    sharepoint_tcs_data_path, "TCS_DispositionsPerCharge_A.xlsx"),
  .name_repair = make_clean_names
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.POSIXct), as.Date))

### import placements
tcs_placements <- read_xlsx(
  file.path(
    sharepoint_tcs_data_path, "TCS_Placements_A.xlsx"),
  .name_repair = make_clean_names
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.POSIXct), as.Date))

### import mandatory events (to explore legal status)
tcs_mandatory_events <- read_xlsx(
  file.path(
    sharepoint_tcs_data_path, "TCS_MandatoryEvents_A.xlsx"),
  .name_repair = make_clean_names
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.POSIXct), as.Date))
```

### 2. De-dup/figure out primary keys for 'cases', 'charges', 'dispositions', and 'placements' and merge together


From Laura, Tanya, and Susan Svoboda:

For TCS, all data sets may be linked with CourtType, Year, TCSReportCourtJCL, CaseYear, CaseID and CaseType.

Juvenile/Name Number is available on the following data sets:
Cases – JuvenileNbr identifies the juvenile for the TCSreportCourtname.  Some of the FJ casetypes do not have a JuvenileNbr because a juvenile record is not created in adult cases.  In adult cases(in this data set only FJ), if the case had a prior juvenile record the JuvenileNbr will be populated indicated a reoffending juvenile in adult court.

Charges – no juvenile name number in data set – link to cases and use Juvenile Nbr, if needed; 1 to many charges can relate to a case.

MandatoryEvents –   NameNbr identifies the juvenile; 1 to many mandatory events will relate to a case.  Key events, legal status set, adjudication, disposition events etc.

Placements - NameNbr identifies the juvenile; 0 to many placement events will relate to a case.  Would recommend using the PCN events and not use ORD.  Courts should be using PCN events.
Financials –   PayorPatyNameNbr identifies the payor party.  This may or may not be the juvenile; 0 to many financial records will relate to a case.  Link to cases and use Juvenile Nbr, if needed.
Program Results – no juvenile name number in data set – link to cases and use Juvenile Nbr, if needed; 0 to many program results can relate to a case.
Sentencing – no juvenile name number in data set – link to cases and use Juvenile Nbr, if needed.


Other notes from Josh M:

•	Missing charge classification for 8.5% of all records in charge data file – clarification on reason
o	Data entry error or city ordinance –
o	Look up Michigan state code –
o	Look at codes with classification and compare to codes without classification
o	By case type – clue b/c it reflects highest charge (fj = felony, dl = not felony juvenile)
•	Coding placement types (see attached Excel for remaining coding questions)
o	Use facility code/rate with public list of facility codes (not all courts use financial data)


•	Clarification on  “Would recommend using the PCN events and not use ORD.  Courts should be using PCN events.” – what is the distinction between the two?
o	ORD – ordered to transport -- temporary
o	PCN – placement change notice


**seemingly important dates:**

* offense_dt
* case_file_dt
* adjudication_dt
* arraignment_dt
* disposition
* case_reopen_dt
* case_closed_dt

<br>

```{r message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
######################################
#### cases
######################################

# de-dup cases file -- there is a very slight discrepancy in N size when de-duping by only juvenile_nbr and case_number as opposed to also including one or more of the above dates; keeping as juvenile_nbr and case_number makes most intuitive sense pending confirmation from JIS contacts (also de-duping by offense_dt as we may need this for later joins...)
tcs_cases_de_dup <- tcs_cases %>%
  filter(!is.na(juvenile_nbr)==TRUE,
         juvenile_nbr!=0, ### there are a handful of records where juvenile_nbr=0; appears to be data error as the records don't consistently share other identifying info like dates and county
         !is.na(case_number)==TRUE) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(case_id = case_number) %>%  ### there are a number of important primary keys which have different names across the files -- here case_id and case_number are the same ID (naming all 'case_id')
  distinct(juvenile_nbr,case_id,court_type,year,tc_sreport_court_jcl,case_year,case_type,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year),
         case_year = as.numeric(year))

### 99% of dropped cases are due to 'caseload_action' -- multiple entries as different stages of case are entered 
```

<br><br>

```{r message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
######################################
#### charges
######################################

# de-dup charges file -- using case_id (same as 'case_number' in tcs_cases and 'id' (which is "Unique ID for the record.")); no records dropped
# note: there are 1,288 records in the cases df that do not appear at all in the charges df; note from Laura and team: "no juvenile name number in data set – link to cases and use Juvenile Nbr, if needed; 1 to many charges can relate to a case."
# case_number identifies case and id uniquely identifies charge within case  
tcs_charges_de_dup <- tcs_charges %>% 
    filter(!is.na(case_id)==TRUE,
         !is.na(id)==TRUE) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(case_number = case_id) %>% 
  distinct(id,case_number,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(current_charge_classification_clean = ifelse(str_starts(current_offense,"712A"),"Status",current_offense_classification)) ### recode status offense (from laura's team: "If you filter on CurrentOffense by 712A – that should give you the status offenses.")
```

<br><br>

```{r message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
######################################
#### dispositions
######################################

# de-dup dispositions file -- using case_id (same as 'case_number' in tcs_cases and 'id' (which is "Unique ID for the record.")); no records dropped -- will have to further de-dup by disposition later

# dropped records are due to each offense having its own disposition row per case per offense/charge (id)
# adding 'id' results in no rows being dropped
tcs_dispositions_de_dup <- tcs_dispositions %>% 
    filter(!is.na(case_id)==TRUE,
         !is.na(name_nbr)==TRUE) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(juvenile_nbr= name_nbr) %>% ### there are a number of important primary keys which have different names across the files -- here name_nbr and juvenile_nbr are the same ID (naming all 'juvenile_nbr')
  distinct(juvenile_nbr,case_id,court_type,year,tc_sreport_court_jcl,case_year,case_type,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(id = as.character(id))
```

<br><br>

```{r message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
######################################
#### placements
######################################

# de-dup placements file -- using case_id (same as 'case_number' in tcs_cases and 'id' (which is "Unique ID for the record.")); no records dropped 
# looks like there are some pure dups
tcs_placements_de_dup <- tcs_placements %>% 
    filter(!is.na(case_id)==TRUE,
         !is.na(name_nbr)==TRUE,
         order_type=="PCN") %>% ### from laura and team: "Would recommend using the PCN events and not use ORD ("ordered to transport"/temporary record).  Courts should be using PCN ("placement change notice") events."
  dplyr::rename(juvenile_nbr= name_nbr) %>% ### there are a number of important primary keys which have different names across the files -- here name_nbr and juvenile_nbr are the same ID (naming all 'juvenile_nbr')
  distinct(juvenile_nbr,case_id,court_type,year,tc_sreport_court_jcl,case_year,case_type,place_begin_date,place_type,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% ### 54 dups (can further de-dup by keeping placement with longer los when dates match)
  mutate(unique_placement_id = paste0(juvenile_nbr,case_id,place_begin_date,place_type,place_end_date),
         unique_case_id = paste0(juvenile_nbr,case_id,case_year,case_type),
         unique_youth_id = paste0(court_type,year,tc_sreport_court_jcl,juvenile_nbr),
         year = as.numeric(year),
         case_year = as.numeric(year)) %>% 
  ungroup()
```

### 3. Start Cleaning w/ Placements (this will serve as base file -- as we interested only in those for whom there is placement data)

Here are our groupings for placement type:
```{r message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
placement_detention <- c("Calhoun County Juvenile Home","DETENTION","I-Child Vill Det (Not VC Disp)","NON-SECURE DETENTION","OTHER COUNTY DETENTION","Regional Detention Center","SECURE DETENTION")

placement_residential_non_mdhhs <- c("I-Boot Camp","I-CFY Ranch","I-Child Vill Residential","I-Child Vill Secure","I-Private Placement","Independent Placement","INSTITUTIONAL/RESIDENTIAL CARE","PRIVATE AGENCY/INSTITUTION","RESIDENTIAL PLACEMENT","CALHOUN TREATMENT CENTER","Residential Treatment Program")

placement_in_home_aftercare <- c("Aftercare/CV","Bond w/Father","Bond w/Mother","Boot Camp Aftercare","CFY Independent Living","Consent Probation/Father","Consent Probation/Mother","Consent Probation/Other","Consent Probation/Parents","Crossroads For Youth Aftercare","CUS","F01","Father","GDN","Guardian","Home of Guardian-Crt Supervsn","Home of Guardian-DHS Sprv.","Home of Guardian-FIA Supervsn","Home of Parent-Crt Supervision","Home of Parent-DHS Supervision","Home of Parent-FIA Supervision","Home of Parent-No Supervision","Home of parent CRT Supervision","Home of Relative-CRT Supervisi","HOME OF RELATIVE-CRT SUPERVSN","Home of Relative-FIA Supervisi","Home of Relative-FIA Supervsn","I-Child Vill Fam Based Reentry","I-Custodian","Intensive Probation/Father","Intensive Probation/Mother","Intensive Probation/Other","Intensive Probation/Parents","Intensive Reentry Parents","Intensive Reentry Program","Intensive Reentry/Father","Intensive Reentry/Mother","Intensive Reentry/Other","M01","Own Home (Both Parents)","Own Home/Father","Own Home/Mother","PARENTS","PLACED WITH PARENT-CRT SPRV","PLACED WITH PARENT-DHS SPRV","PLACED WITH RELATIVE-CRT SPRV","Probation/Father","Bond w/Parent", "Probation/Mother","Probation/Other","Probation/Parents","PTS","REL","Relative","Relative Placement","Unrelated Unlicensed Home","CFY Day Stud","CFY Work Ed Day St")

placement_mdhhs <- c("DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SERVICES","DSS","Family Independence Agency","I-Department of Human Services","I-DHHS-150/Del")

placement_awol <- c("Absent without Leave","Order Take Into Custody")

placement_jail <- c("I-Oakland County Jail","Jail")

placement_foster_shelter <- c("Foster Care-Court Supervision","Foster Care-FIA Supervision","PLACED IN FOSTER CARE-DHS SPRV","PLACED IN FOSTER CARE-CRT SPRV","Shelter Home")
```

<br><br>

Create clean placement categories 
```{r message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
tcs_placements_de_dup %<>%
  mutate(place_type_clean = 
           case_when(
             place_type_desc %in% placement_detention ~ 1,
             place_type_desc %in% placement_residential_non_mdhhs ~ 2,
             place_type_desc %in% placement_mdhhs ~ 3,
             place_type_desc %in% placement_jail ~ 4,
             place_type_desc %in% placement_awol ~ 5,
             place_type_desc %in% placement_in_home_aftercare ~ 6,
             place_type_desc %in% placement_foster_shelter ~ 7,
             TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
         place_type_clean = factor(place_type_clean,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7),
         labels = c("Detention","Residential","MDHHS","Jail","AWOL","In Home/Aftercare","Foster Care/Shelter Home"))) %>% ### use factor function to assign labels to values
  ungroup()
```

### Individual Placements: Counts and Percentages, 2016-2020
```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
tcs_placements_de_dup_ind_place_denom <- tcs_placements_de_dup %>% 
  filter(case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018,2019,2020),
         !is.na(place_type_clean)==TRUE) %>% ### only looking at earlier years because we don't want to artificially deflate the median
  summarise(`Sample N` = n_distinct(unique_placement_id)) 

tcs_placements_de_dup_ind_place_grouped <- tcs_placements_de_dup %>% 
  filter(case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018,2019,2020),
         !is.na(place_type_clean)==TRUE) %>% ### only looking at earlier years because we don't want to artificially deflate the median
  distinct(unique_placement_id, .keep_all=TRUE) %>% 
  group_by(place_type_clean) %>% 
  summarise(`Sample N` = n_distinct(unique_placement_id), 
            `Sample %` = round(n_distinct(unique_placement_id)/tcs_placements_de_dup_ind_place_denom$`Sample N`*100, digits = 1)) %>% 
  ungroup()
```

Calculate length of stay and create LOS buckets (for possible calculation by individual placement and within case)
```{r message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### calculate length of stay in three different ways:
# los with everything counted 
# los split into placement type buckets -- making sure to recode '0' as NA so as to not bring down mean LOS when youth was never actually placed somewhere
tcs_placements_de_dup %<>%
  group_by(unique_case_id) %>% ### group by case
  mutate(case_first_place_date = min(place_begin_date),
         case_last_place_date = max(place_end_date)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(unique_placement_los = time_length(difftime(place_end_date, place_begin_date), unit = 'days'),
         los_unique_placement_detention_only = ifelse(place_type_clean=="Detention",unique_placement_los,NA),
         los_unique_placement_residential_non_mdhhs_only = ifelse(place_type_clean=="Residential",unique_placement_los,NA),
         los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only = ifelse(place_type_clean=="MDHHS",unique_placement_los,NA)) %>% 
  group_by(unique_case_id) %>% 
  mutate(los_case_overall_all_included = sum(unique_placement_los),
         los_case_overall_all_included = ifelse(los_case_overall_all_included==0,NA,los_case_overall_all_included),
         los_overall_detention_only = sum(los_unique_placement_detention_only),
         los_overall_detention_only = ifelse(los_overall_detention_only==0,NA,los_overall_detention_only),
         los_overall_residential_only = sum(los_unique_placement_residential_non_mdhhs_only),
         los_overall_residential_only = ifelse(los_overall_residential_only==0,NA,los_overall_residential_only),
         los_overall_mdhhs_only = sum(los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only),
         los_overall_mdhhs_only = ifelse(los_overall_mdhhs_only==0,NA,los_overall_mdhhs_only)) %>% 
  ungroup()

### create grouped los bins for detention
### mirror becky's approach with the kalamazoo analysis
### recode LOS_placement (1/3=1 "1-3 days") (4/7=2 "4-7 days") (8/14=3 "8-14 days") (15/30=4 "15-30 days") (31/90=5 "1-3 months") (91/max=6 ">3 months"), gen (placement_buckets)
tcs_placements_de_dup %<>%
  mutate(los_unique_placement_detention_only_grouped_bin = case_when(
    los_unique_placement_detention_only<3 & los_unique_placement_detention_only!=0 ~ 1,
    los_unique_placement_detention_only>=3 & los_unique_placement_detention_only<7 ~ 2,
    los_unique_placement_detention_only>=7 & los_unique_placement_detention_only<15 ~ 3,
    los_unique_placement_detention_only>=15 & los_unique_placement_detention_only<=30 ~ 4,
    los_unique_placement_detention_only>=30 & los_unique_placement_detention_only<=90 ~ 5,
    los_unique_placement_detention_only>90 ~ 6,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    los_unique_placement_detention_only_grouped_bin = factor(los_unique_placement_detention_only_grouped_bin,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5,6),
         labels = c("1 to 3 Days", "3 to 7 Days", "7 to 14 Days","15 to 30 Days","30 to 90 Days","90 Days+"))) ### use factor function to assign labels to values

### create grouped los bins for residential placement
tcs_placements_de_dup %<>%
  mutate(los_unique_placement_residential_only_grouped_bin = case_when(
    los_unique_placement_residential_non_mdhhs_only<32 & los_unique_placement_residential_non_mdhhs_only!=0 ~ 1,
    los_unique_placement_residential_non_mdhhs_only>=32 & los_unique_placement_residential_non_mdhhs_only<92 ~ 2,
    los_unique_placement_residential_non_mdhhs_only>=92 & los_unique_placement_residential_non_mdhhs_only<=275 ~ 3,
    los_unique_placement_residential_non_mdhhs_only>=275 & los_unique_placement_residential_non_mdhhs_only<=549 ~ 4,
    los_unique_placement_residential_non_mdhhs_only>549 ~ 5,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    los_unique_placement_residential_only_grouped_bin = factor(los_unique_placement_residential_only_grouped_bin,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5),
         labels = c("Less than 1 Month", "1 to 3 Months","3 to 9 Months","9 to 18 Months","18 Months+"))) ### use factor function to assign labels to values

### create grouped los bins for mdhhs placement
tcs_placements_de_dup %<>%
  mutate(los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only_grouped_bin = case_when(
    los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only<32 & los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only!=0 ~ 1,
    los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only>=32 & los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only<92 ~ 2,
    los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only>=92 & los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only<=275 ~ 3,
    los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only>=275 & los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only<=549 ~ 4,
    los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only>549 ~ 5,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only_grouped_bin = factor(los_unique_placement_mdhhs_only_grouped_bin,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5),
         labels = c("Less than 1 Month", "1 to 3 Months","3 to 9 Months","9 to 18 Months","18 Months+"))) ### use factor function to assign labels to values
```

### Median LOS -- Detention, Residential, and Treatment, 2016-2018 (individual placements)
```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
tcs_placements_de_dup_median_ind_place <- tcs_placements_de_dup %>% 
  filter(case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018),
         !is.na(place_type_clean)==TRUE) %>% ### only looking at earlier years because we don't want to artificially deflate the median
  distinct(unique_placement_id,.keep_all=TRUE) %>% 
  group_by(place_type_clean) %>% 
  summarise(`Median Length of Stay, Sample N` = n_distinct(unique_placement_id[!is.na(unique_placement_los)==TRUE]), 
            `Median Length of Stay, Days` = round(median(unique_placement_los, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 0)) %>% 
  ungroup()
```

### Clean race/ethnicity in `placements` and `cases` data frame

From Laura and team:

From TCS  
•	AI-American Indian  
•	BR-Bi-Racial 
•	OT-Other  
•	BA-Black American  
•	OA-Oriental American  
•	SA-Spanish American  
•	WA-White American  
•	A-Asian American  
•	AF-African/American  
•	AR-Arabic  
•	C-Caucasian  
•	H-Hispanic  
•	CH-Chinese  
•	K-Korean  
•	MR-Multi-Racial  
•	R-Russian  
•	RO-Romanian  
•	HI-Native Hawaiian  

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
### placements
tcs_placements_de_dup %<>%
  mutate(race_csg_6 = case_when(
    race %in% c("OA","A","CH","K","HI") ~ 1,
    race %in% c("BA","AF") ~ 2,
    race %in% c("SA","H") ~ 3,
    race %in% c("WA","Caucasian","Russian","Romanian") ~ 4,
    race %in% c("AI") ~ 5,
    race %in% c("BR","OT","AR","MR") ~ 6,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    race_csg_6 = factor(race_csg_6,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5,6),
         labels = c("Asian/Native Hawaiian", "Black", "Hispanic", "White","American Indian", "Multi Racial/Other"))) %>% ### use factor function to assign labels to values)
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(gender_clean = case_when( ### there are six records for which there is an 'unknown' value and 44 missing records -- i am grouping these together here
    gender=="F" ~ 1,
    gender=="M" ~ 2,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    gender_clean = factor(gender_clean,
         levels = c(1,2),
         labels = c("Female", "Male"))) ### use factor function to assign labels to values

### cases
tcs_cases_de_dup %<>%
  mutate(race_csg_6 = case_when(
    defendant_race %in% c("OA","A","CH","K","HI") ~ 1,
    defendant_race %in% c("BA","AF") ~ 2,
    defendant_race %in% c("SA","H") ~ 3,
    defendant_race %in% c("WA","Caucasian","Russian","Romanian") ~ 4,
    defendant_race %in% c("AI") ~ 5,
    defendant_race %in% c("BR","OT","AR","MR") ~ 6,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    race_csg_6 = factor(race_csg_6,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5,6),
         labels = c("Asian/Native Hawaiian", "Black", "Hispanic", "White","American Indian", "Multi Racial/Other"))) ### use factor function to assign labels to values)
```

### Individual placements per 10k youth by county, 2016-2020
```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### clean county name -- extracting county name
tcs_placements_de_dup %<>%
  mutate(county_name = word(tc_sreport_courtname, 1),
         county_name = str_to_title(county_name),
         county_court_name = str_to_title(county_name))

### import ezapop race/ethnicity data for 10-17 y/o michigan residents for rate calculation
df_ezapop_race_ethnicity_10_17_county_level <- readr::read_delim("C:\\Users\\abyrum\\The Council of State Governments\\JC Research - Documents\\JC Research - JJ_Michigan - JJ_Michigan\\Data\\Ezapop\\ezapop_10_17_race_eth_sex_mi.txt", delim = "|") %>% 
  mutate(county_name =  gsub(" County", "", county_name)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(county_name,overall_10_17_population)

### create overall file for numerator in % calculation below
tcs_placements_de_dup_county <- tcs_placements_de_dup %>% 
  filter(case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018,2019,2020),
         !is.na(county_name)==TRUE) %>% 
  distinct(unique_placement_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% ### de-dup by person and placement episode since we want to take the mean of a value duplicated across all placements within placement episode; we want one record per youth per placement episode where there is county data
  group_by(county_name) %>% 
  summarize(placement_case_count = n_distinct(unique_placement_id[place_type_clean %in% c("Residential","MDHHS")])) %>% ### either los_overall_residential_only or los_overall_mdhhs_only must have a LOS to be counted as a "case with placement" here -- josh w's definition
  ungroup() %>% 
  left_join(df_ezapop_race_ethnicity_10_17_county_level, by = "county_name") %>% 
  mutate(placements_per_10k_youth = round(placement_case_count/overall_10_17_population*10000, digits = 1))

### create quantiles object
no_classes <- 4

### extract quantiles from var we're mapping
quantiles <- tcs_placements_de_dup_county %>%
  pull(placements_per_10k_youth) %>%
  quantile(probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = no_classes + 1), na.rm=TRUE) %>%
  as.vector() 

### make labels youth pop
label_place_rate <- c("106.5 to 186.5","36.9 to 106.5","28.4 to 36.9", "0 to 28.4")

### create a new variable with the specified quantiles
tcs_placements_de_dup_county %<>%
  mutate(placements_per_10k_youth_quartile = cut(-placements_per_10k_youth,
                               breaks = -quantiles,
                               right = TRUE,
                               labels = label_place_rate,
                               include.lowest = T)) %>% 
  mutate(county_anonymous = paste0("County ", row_number())) 


### plot
ggplot(data = tcs_placements_de_dup_county,
            mapping = aes(x = reorder(county_anonymous, placements_per_10k_youth), y = placements_per_10k_youth, fill = placements_per_10k_youth_quartile)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "gray40") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#00475d","#007392","#0db4e4","#9ed4ef")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(min(0), 
                                           max(195))) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = scales::wrap_format(18)) +
  annotate("text", x = 5, y = 150, label = "Each bar represents one county's\n individual placement rate", colour = "#00475d", size = 4) +
    theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          # panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.line=element_blank(),
          legend.position = "top",
        legend.title.align=0.5,
        axis.text.y=element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y=element_blank()) +
    labs(y = NULL, x = NULL,
      caption = NULL,
      title = NULL,
      subtitle = NULL,
      fill = "Residential or MDHHS Placements\nper 10k Youth") +
    coord_flip() +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = FALSE)) 
```

#### Placement N's: Unique Placements by County (County Court), cases filed 2016-2020 

Note: Placements in this table are individual placements, not grouped by individual or case

Question: Do all Michigan counties have their own court? We don't appear to have county of residence for youth so if multiple counties share one court, they would be grouped together here. We have one extra county -- GOGEBIC -- in the case data but not in the placement data
```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### create overall placement count denominator for % in cross-tabs
unique_placement_id_n <- n_distinct(tcs_placements_de_dup$unique_placement_id[!is.na(tcs_placements_de_dup$county_court_name)==TRUE])

### all -- grouped by placement type
tcs_placements_place_type <- tcs_placements_de_dup %>% 
  distinct(unique_placement_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(county_court_name)==TRUE,
         case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018,2019,2020)) %>% 
  group_by(county_court_name) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(unique_placement_id),
            `Percent of Total (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_placement_id)/unique_placement_id_n*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(`County Court` = county_court_name) %>% 
  mutate(`County Court` = as.character(`County Court`))

### all -- overall
tcs_placements_place_type_overall <- tcs_placements_de_dup %>% 
  distinct(unique_placement_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(county_court_name)==TRUE,
         case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018,2019,2020)) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(unique_placement_id),
            `Percent of Total (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_placement_id)/unique_placement_id_n*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(`County Court` = "Overall") 

### combine tables for kable
tcs_placements_place_type_table <- rbind(tcs_placements_place_type,tcs_placements_place_type_overall)

### print table via kableextra
kable(tcs_placements_place_type_table, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), align=rep('c')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"), row_label_position = "l") %>% 
  row_spec(10, bold = TRUE)
```

#### Placement N's: Unique Placements by Missing Start and/or End Date

Note: Placements in this table are individual placements, not grouped by individual or case
```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### create overall placement count denominator for % in cross-tabs
unique_placement_id_n <- n_distinct(tcs_placements_de_dup$unique_placement_id)

### create flag for missing start or end date
tcs_placements_de_dup %<>%
  mutate(missing_start_end_date = ifelse((is.na(place_begin_date)== TRUE | is.na(place_end_date)==TRUE),"Missing at least one date","Not missing any dates"))

### all -- grouped by placement type
tcs_placements_place_type <- tcs_placements_de_dup %>% 
  distinct(unique_placement_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(missing_start_end_date)==TRUE) %>% 
  group_by(missing_start_end_date) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(unique_placement_id),
            `Percent of Total (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_placement_id)/unique_placement_id_n*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(`Missing Date` = missing_start_end_date) %>% 
  mutate(`Missing Date` = as.character(`Missing Date`))

### all -- overall
tcs_placements_place_type_overall <- tcs_placements_de_dup %>% 
  distinct(unique_placement_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(place_type_desc)==TRUE) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(unique_placement_id),
            `Percent of Total (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_placement_id)/unique_placement_id_n*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(`Missing Date` = "Overall")
```

#### Charge N's: Unique Placements by Placement/Facility Type, cases filed 2016-2020 

Note: Charges in this table are individual charges, not grouped by individual or case. These are not yet linked to placements -- this is simply the universe of charges in the TCS data. 

```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
# From TCS code book: Current Offense Classification - C/Civil Infraction, F/Felony, M/Misdemeanor, S/Statute, H/High Misdemeanor, O/Other, V/Civil-Other, R/Ordinance, Z/Notice for Advisories
tcs_charges_de_dup %<>%
  mutate(current_offense_classification_clean = case_when(
    current_offense_classification %in% c("C","V") ~ 1,
    current_offense_classification == "F" ~ 2,
    current_offense_classification == "M" ~ 3,
    current_offense_classification == "S" ~ 4,
    current_offense_classification == "H" ~ 5,
    current_offense_classification == "R" ~ 6,
    current_offense_classification == "Z" ~ 7,
    current_offense_classification == "O" ~ 8,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    current_offense_classification_clean = factor(current_offense_classification_clean,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8),
         labels = c("Civil","Felony", "Misdemeanor","Statute","High Misdemeanor","Ordinance","Notice for Advisories","Other"))) %>% ### use factor function to assign labels to values)
  mutate(unique_charge_id = paste0(id,case_number))

### create overall placement count denominator for % in cross-tabs
unique_charge_id_n <- n_distinct(tcs_charges_de_dup$unique_charge_id[!is.na(tcs_charges_de_dup$current_offense_classification_clean)==TRUE])

### all -- grouped by placement type
tcs_charge_type <- tcs_charges_de_dup %>% 
  distinct(unique_charge_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(current_offense_classification_clean)==TRUE,
         case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018,2019,2020)) %>% 
  group_by(current_offense_classification_clean) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(unique_charge_id),
            `Percent of Total (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_charge_id)/unique_charge_id_n*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(`Charge Classification` = current_offense_classification_clean) %>% 
  mutate(`Charge Classification` = as.character(`Charge Classification`))

### all -- overall
tcs_charge_type_overall <- tcs_charges_de_dup %>% 
  distinct(unique_charge_id,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(current_offense_classification_clean)==TRUE,
         case_year%in%c(2016,2017,2018,2019,2020)) %>% 
  summarise(`Unique Count (N)` = n_distinct(unique_charge_id),
            `Percent of Total (%)` = round(n_distinct(unique_charge_id)/unique_charge_id_n*100, digits = 2)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(`Charge Classification` = "Overall") 

### combine tables for kable
tcs_charge_type_table <- rbind(tcs_charge_type,tcs_charge_type_overall)

### print table via kableextra
kable(tcs_charge_type_table, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), align=rep('c')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"), row_label_position = "l") %>% 
  row_spec(6, bold = TRUE)
```

## Codebooks

<br>

#### Cases
```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### disable scientific notation
options(scipen=999)

### import variable labels from 'CSG_TCS_DataDictionary FINAL'
cases_labels <- readxl::read_xlsx(file.path(
    sharepoint_tcs_data_path, "CSG_TCS_DataDictionary FINAL.xlsx"),
  .name_repair = make_clean_names,
  sheet ="Cases", range = "B2:C110") %>% 
  mutate(data_column = make_clean_names(data_column))

### get descriptive statistics and select those of interest
cases_descriptives <- tcs_cases_de_dup %>% 
  describe(.,
           check = FALSE) %>% 
  mutate(data_column = row.names(.)) %>% 
  as_tibble() %>% 
  select(data_column,"n","min","max","mean") %>% 
  mutate(data_column = stringr::str_replace(data_column,"\\*",""))

### add stats to label 
cases_codebook <- left_join(cases_descriptives,cases_labels,by="data_column") %>% 
  select(data_column,tcs_definition=definition,everything())

### print table via kableextra
kable(cases_codebook, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), align=rep('c')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"), 
                row_label_position = "l") 
```

## Main Questions (out to Laura/relevant staff)

1.	Construction of ‘juvenile_nbr’ in ‘cases’ data file and ‘name_nbr’ in in ‘dispositions’ and ‘placements’ data files:
a.	These appear to all be the same column – is this column created just from a youth’s name? If so, should we use it in together with one of the age variables – such as ‘defendant_age_at_filing’ – to uniquely identify one youth (essentially a roundabout way of using name and DOB)? Any caution against this approach?
b.	I see a small number of ‘juvenile_nbr’ values of 0 – I have initially dropped these records as they don’t appear to the same individual. Is that correct? 


2.	In looking through the raw data, there appear to be instances in which one ‘case_number’/’caseid’ (these appear to be the same field) is shared by more than one ‘juvenile_nbr’/’name_nbr’. Why would this be the case? And is the joint use of both ‘case_number’/’caseid’ and ‘juvenile_nbr’/’name_nbr’ the best way to uniquely identify a single case?
a.	What is the definition/business rule for ‘case_number’/’caseid’? When are two offenses grouped as one ‘case_number’ and when would they appear as separate cases? 


3.	For our analysis of placement data in the TCS transfer, we are hoping to merge 'cases', 'charges', 'dispositions', and 'placements' together. Is this possible/advisable? 
a.	It appears as though there are ‘juvenile_nbr’/’name_nbr’s and ‘case_number’/’caseid’s which appear in the ‘cases’ and ‘placements’ data tables, but not in the ‘charges’ data table. Do you all have any initial ideas for why this may be? 
b.	In general, it looks like we would merge these data files using ‘juvenile_nbr’/’name_nbr’ and ‘case_number’/’caseid’ (and then ‘id’ can additionally be used to link ‘charges’ and ‘dispositions’ – does this make sense? Are there better ways to determine primary keys, de-duplicate (if need be), and merge? 


4.	What is the difference between `case_year` (noted as the "Year the case was filed.") and `year` (noted as "Year of the caseload being run/reported.")? Why does the data dictionary indicate that `year` "Must be included in some form to link tables" but not `case_year`?


5.	Is there a code book/data dictionary available for column values – particularly for race/ethnicity, event_nbr, dispo_event_nbr, sequence_nbr, case_type


6.	What is `ordertype` in the ‘placements’ data file? Many records with value of `ORD` as opposed to `PCN` are missing either start dates and/or end dates – why is this the case?
